title: Grandma’s Pickles

items.raw: 2 pounds (900 g) small Kirby pickling cucumbers, 3–4 inches long
1½ cups (355 ml) distilled white vinegar, 5% acidity
2 tablespoons (36 g) pickling or canning salt
4 large fresh dill heads, or a generous handful of dill sprigs plus 2 teaspoons dill seed
2 grape leaves or bay leaves (optional, for crunch)

steps.text: Scrub the cucumbers under cold water and trim ⅛ inch off the blossom end — the end opposite the stem. It holds an enzyme that softens pickles. Soak them in ice water for 30 minutes while you make the brine.
Bring the water, vinegar, salt, and sugar to a boil in a saucepan, stirring until the salt dissolves. Let it cool for 10 minutes.
Divide the garlic, dill, mustard seed, peppercorns, pepper flakes, and leaves between two clean quart jars. Pack the cucumbers in tightly, upright, whole or cut into spears.
Pour the warm brine over the cucumbers until they are fully submerged, leaving ½ inch at the top. Tap the jars to release air bubbles, then close them.
Let the jars cool to room temperature, then refrigerate. They are pickled after 2 to 3 days, and better still after a week.

notes.label: Use pickling salt
notes.text: table salt contains anti-caking agents that cloud the brine. Kosher salt works, but brands weigh differently, so measure it by weight (36 g).

notes.label: Storage
notes.text: keep refrigerated and eat within 1 month. These are not shelf-stable.

notes.label: For the pantry
notes.text: if Grandma canned hers, follow a tested canning recipe (USDA or Ball) exactly. Those use a specific brine and water-bath processing — typically 10 minutes for pints and 15 for quarts.

notes.label: Variations
notes.text: spears or coins pickle faster than whole cucumbers. Bread-and-butter pickles use a sweeter brine with onion and turmeric.

openQuestion: This is a best guess — classic garlicky dill pickles kept in the refrigerator. We don’t know whether Grandma’s pickles were dill, bread-and-butter, or sour, or whether she canned them for the pantry. Tell me which, and anything you remember about how they were cut, what was in the jar, and when she made them.
